commitResults.messageTitle: Ask for the contact's index when picking a duplicate
commitResults.messageBody:
When a name matches several contacts, delete, drop and introduce list
the candidates and prompt "Enter a contact number". Astra also calls
the phone number a contact number, so users could reasonably type a
phone number instead of the displayed index.

Let's ask for the index of the contact instead, and share one prompt
between the drop and person selection requests so the two cannot
drift apart again.

The user guide still said drop makes no changes and introduce asks
the user to retry, although both now let the user pick a candidate.
Let's describe the selection step for both commands.

Fixes #298.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop fuzzy find matching unrelated short names
commitResults.messageBody:
find /fuzzy accepts any name word within two edits of the query. A
query of one or two letters can be rewritten into any short word in
two edits, so find /fuzzy Al lists Bernice Yu and David Li although
they share no letter with the query.

Let's allow at most one edit fewer than the query's length, keeping
the two-edit limit for longer queries. Typos such as Jhon for John
and Alicee for Alice still match.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: List every add and find option in their usage text
commitResults.messageBody:
The usage text shown after an invalid add or find command leaves out
options the parsers accept:

* add omits ev/EVENT, so a blank ev/ is rejected with a usage text
  that does not mention the prefix the user typed.
* find omits /fuzzy and /event, so users who mistype either search
  are not told the option exists.

Let's list these options, matching the user guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept accented names and reject non-digit phones
commitResults.messageBody:
Name validation rejects names whose letters carry combining marks, such
as Devanagari vowel signs or an accent typed as a separate character,
although NFR 9 promises names in any language. Phone validation accepts
numerals such as 1/2 or superscripts, which are not digits.

Let's allow combining marks after a name's first character and accept
only decimal digits in phone numbers, with regression tests for both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
